title: Electorate of Salzburg
capsule: The Electorate of Salzburg was a lay principality created by the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss of 1803, which secularised the ancient Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg and assigned it to Archduke Ferdinand III of Austria (deposed Grand Duke of Tuscany) as compensation for his loss of Florence. Ferdinand was its sole ruler; he introduced enlightened administrative reforms during his brief tenure. The electorate was extinguished by the Peace of Pressburg (26 December 1805) after Austria's defeat at Austerlitz: Salzburg itself reverted to Austria, while other portions went to Bavaria, and Ferdinand received the new Electorate of Würzburg in exchange.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territory is precisely defined by the 1803 Reichsdeputationshauptschluss and the 1805 Peace of Pressburg; extent is certain.
